'''KP-1''' was a [[Gender|masculine]] [[K-series]] [[astromech droid]]<ref name="Build My Droid article" /> associated with the [[Hidden Path]].<ref name="Kenobi V" /> In [[9 BBY]],<ref name="Kenobi date">{{KenobiDate|V}}</ref> the [[droid]] was found on the [[planet]] [[Jabiim]].<ref name="Kenobi V" />

{{Char-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The idea was, 'A salty breath of fresh air.' Salty at times, but you're always happy to have him by your side|Camille Manet describing the idea for KP-1|<ref name="Build My Droid article" />}}
KP-1 first appeared in "[[Part V]]," the fifth episode of the ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'' television series,<ref name="Kenobi V" /> which was released on [[June 15]], [[2022]].<ref name="D23">{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-june-2022|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in June 2022}}</ref> KP-1 was designed by [[Camille Manet]], the winner of the [[Build My Droid]] contest held in [[2019]].<ref name="Contest winner">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-build-my-droid-contest-winner|text=Meet KP-1, Winner of the ''Star Wars'' 'Build My Droid' Contest}}</ref>

[[File:KP-1FinalSketch.png|thumb|right|260px|Camille Manet's final sketch of KP-1]]
Manet joined the contest after the [[sequel trilogy]] awakened her interest in the ''[[Star Wars]]''<ref name="Build My Droid article" /> and she realized she subconsciously thought of a drawing of a droid that could be helpful in her daily life.<ref name="BMD Contest">{{SWYouTube|QrSKKyWhZvU|Build My Droid Contest | Obi-Wan Kenobi | Disney+}}</ref> Manet then started to design the droid KP-1 whose name is short for "Knave Puff." During the design phase, she realized that coming up with something original that fit the ''Star Wars'' aesthetic would be key. Manet wanted to find a balance between the long tradition of droids people are familiar with and something entirely new.<ref name="Build My Droid article" /> She aimed to create a concept that showed innovation because she felt the attention granted to details and specificity binded the cinematic universe together. Manet struggled to come up with the basic shape before coming up with the persona.<ref name="Contest winner" /> The droid's cone head was a new idea and made KP-1's silhouette identifiable, however the classic astromech dome grounded the design in ''Star Wars''. Manet had the wheel as a design starting point and then thought of putting it horizontally, and she thought that retractable arms could be on the wheel. Manet added [[Color|pink]] body and red accents because she liked the color combination. She wanted to differentiate KP-1 from famous droids, so she purposely avoided blue, gold, and orange because those colors are associated with [[R2-D2]], [[C-3PO]], and [[BB-8]], respectively.<ref name="Build My Droid article" /> The final sketch included detailed notes on the droid's physical dimensions and his array of tools.<ref name="Contest winner" /> Manet also wrote an essay about KP-1.<ref name="BMD Contest" />

The droid's playful yet temperamental demeanor was inspired by famous ''Star Wars'' droids. Manet imagined her droid expressing all emotions and sums up KP-1's character as "salty." Manet wanted the name to reflect the droid's character: "clever and insightful, always a step ahead, a dash of mischievousness, and as you can't predict where a breath of fresh air will blow, a tad bit unpredictable; a surprise, for sure, but a welcome one."<ref name="Contest winner" /> The idea was also KP-1 was salty at times, but people would always be happy to have him by their side."<ref name="Build My Droid article" /> She also wanted KP-1 to very loyal and easily offended, but not for long, and he will always be determined to carry out his mission.<ref name="Contest winner" />

[[File:KP-1BeingConstructed.png|thumb|left|280px|KP-1 being constructed]]
Manet was later named the grand prize winner of the Build My Droid contest.<ref name="Build My Droid article" /> Lucasfilm art director [[Doug Chiang]] loved Manet's concept of KP-1. During production of ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'', Chiang, director [[Deborah Chow]], and other crew members met virtually to discuss what purpose KP-1 could serve in the show. Chow suggested that the droid could be put in the "pseudo rebel base" and have some functionality. She told the builders to think of the droid's personality as "a scrappy little fighter." Chiang wanted to preserve all of the key elements in the concept and also bring practicality so that it could interact with the actors. Chiang and the art department did a drawing of KP-1 over Manet's drawing. The droid's head, [[Photoreceptor|eye]], and markings were modeled after an [[R2-series astromech droid|R2 series astromech droid]].<ref name="BMD Contest">{{SWYouTube|QrSKKyWhZvU|Build My Droid Contest | Obi-Wan Kenobi | Disney+}}</ref> Manet received some updates from Lucasfilm discussing the development of her droid. She also met virtually with Chiang who put some finishing touches on KP-1 for filming. Lucasfilm also showed Manet behind-the-scenes photos and videos of the making of KP-1, including painting, 3D-printing, and the final build in the creature shop. The final form's colors ended up being green and tan, but the overall appearance ended up being almost exact to Manet's vision.<ref name="Build My Droid article" />
